stem:
Form 3 pupils set up four potometers, each with a similar leafy bean shoot, and recorded how far the air bubble moved in 5 minutes.

| Set-up | Conditions | Distance moved by bubble in 5 min (mm) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | Shade, still air | 9 |
| B | Shade, electric fan | 33 |
| C | Bright light, still air | 21 |
| D | Shade, still air, shoot in a clear plastic bag | 3 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the rate of water uptake in set-up B, in mm per minute.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the percentage increase in the distance moved in B compared with A, to the nearest whole number.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Name the factor that was changed in set-up D.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Through which structures is most of the water lost from the shoots?

options.rationale: Correct: water vapour diffuses out through them.
The shoots have no roots, and root hairs absorb water.
Only a little water is lost through the cuticle.

parts.explanation: Most transpiration is through the stomata.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain the result for set-up C compared with set-up A.

points.description: Bright light makes the stomata open wider (and warms the leaves).
So more water vapour diffuses out and the shoot takes up water faster.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Suggest **three** ways in which a farmer could reduce water loss from newly transplanted cabbage seedlings.

points.description: Transplant in the late afternoon or on a cloudy day.
Shade the seedlings / plant windbreaks to reduce wind.
Mulch and water immediately after transplanting.

parts.explanation: Apply the factors to the field.

explanation: Rates from the table; wind, light and humidity change transpiration; apply to transplanting.
hints: Compare each set-up with set-up A.

stem:
Tatenda tested saved maize seed by placing four lots of 50 seeds on moist paper in a warm room for 7 days.

| Lot | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Seeds germinated (out of 50) | 46 | 44 | 47 | 43 |

He also set up three test tubes of soaked seeds: X on moist cotton wool at room temperature; Y under boiled, cooled water covered with oil; Z on moist cotton wool in a refrigerator. Only the seeds in X germinated.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the total number of seeds that germinated.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the percentage germination of the seed.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Which tube shows that oxygen is needed for germination?

options.rationale: X is the control with all conditions.
Z shows the need for a suitable temperature.
X is the control and Z lacks warmth; neither lacks oxygen.
Correct: boiled water and oil exclude oxygen.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Name the condition that was lacking in tube Z.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain why water is needed for germination.

points.description: It softens the testa so the seed swells and the coat splits.
It activates enzymes that digest the stored food / carries dissolved food to the embryo.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Distinguish between germination and emergence.

points.description: Germination: the embryo resumes growth and the radicle breaks through the seed coat (in the soil).
Emergence: the shoot appears above the soil surface.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Suggest **two** reasons why fewer seedlings may emerge in the field than germinated in the test.

points.description: A hard cap on the soil surface / planting too deep.
Cold or waterlogged soil / soil pests or fungi / birds eating the seed.

explanation: A germination test gives viability; tubes show the conditions; field emergence can be lower.
hints: Each tube lacks one condition compared with X.

stem: In cattle, the allele for polled (P) is dominant to the allele for horned (p). A farmer mates polled cows that are heterozygous with a heterozygous polled bull. 64 calves are born.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State the genotype of a horned calf.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Use a genetic diagram to show the expected genotypes and phenotypes of the calves.

points.description: Gametes: P and p from each parent.
Offspring genotypes: 1 PP : 2 Pp : 1 pp.
Phenotypes: 3 polled : 1 horned.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the number of horned calves expected.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the number of heterozygous polled calves expected.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: To find out whether a polled calf is PP or Pp, it should be mated with:

options.rationale: All offspring would be polled whatever its genotype.
Possible but much harder to interpret.
Correct: this is a test cross.
This is inbreeding, not a test cross.

parts.explanation: A homozygous recessive partner reveals any p allele.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Explain why a breeder of polled cattle wants bulls that are homozygous (PP).

points.description: A PP bull passes only P to every calf.
So all his calves are polled whatever the cow's genotype.
A Pp bull passes p to half his calves, so horned calves appear when mated with carrier or horned cows.

explanation: Pp × Pp gives 3 polled : 1 horned; test crosses identify homozygous breeding stock.
hints: Draw the Punnett square for Pp × Pp.
A test cross uses a homozygous recessive partner.

stem: In a fictional seed-company trial, inbred maize line A yielded 2.5 t/ha, inbred line B 3.1 t/ha and the single cross A × B 7.28 t/ha. On a nearby farm, a hybrid crop yielded 7.0 t/ha and grain saved from it and replanted the next season yielded 5.6 t/ha.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Name the type of hybrid produced by crossing a single cross (A × B) with a third inbred line C.
parts.explanation: (A × B) × C is a three-way cross.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Why are the tassels removed from the female rows of a hybrid seed field?

options.content: To reduce the spread of stalk borer
So all silks get pollen from the male rows
To make the cobs grow larger
So the male rows can be harvested
options.rationale: Seed comes from the female rows.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the heterosis of the single cross as a percentage above the mean yield of its parents.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the percentage fall in yield when the hybrid grain was replanted.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain why the yield fell when the hybrid grain was replanted.

points.description: The saved grain is the F2, in which alleles segregate.
Plants vary, many resemble the weaker inbreds and hybrid vigour is lost.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Suggest **three** reasons why some farmers still grow open-pollinated varieties.

points.description: Seed can be saved and replanted, so it is cheap.
Hybrid seed must be bought every season and may be unaffordable or unavailable.
OPVs may be better adapted to low-input, dry conditions / farmers prefer their taste or storage qualities.

explanation: Calculate heterosis and the F2 fall, and link them to seed choice.
hints: Heterosis = (F1 − mean of parents) ÷ mean of parents × 100.
The saved grain is the F2.
